fzImpact.title: FeverZone impact
fzImpact.summary: B2BM is built on FeverZone — most Organizer + System work lands in FZ. The business/IAM + pricing refactors are the spine (and riskiest: they alter live partner data and the booking price path). Publishing / B2B Sales / Sales Ops are net-new surfaces on top. PRD constraint: reconstructing FZ features and integrating legacy capabilities with the Marketplace is a known technical risk; the distributor-facing Marketplace is comparatively greenfield. Discovery/search reuses the B2C Marketplace engine (indexing/search/ranking) — integrate, don't rebuild — surfaced in FeverZone; orgs/IAM, pricing, booking and invoicing remain the new B2BM build (not FeverZone).

refactors.change: Business → Organization (admins/members/roles, shared access, one user in many orgs) + channel-per-plan. Touches login/auth, b2b-iam permissions, FZ business-management surfaces.
Dedicated b2b-marketplace price list; B2B discount % at 4 specificity levels + ticket-type granularity; resolution cascade at booking (SYS-01); price-list↔channel linkage.

B2BM reservations live inside FZ (no separate surface); B2B-portal channel type for reservation rules; reschedule/modify/cancel rules; price-masking on tickets (SYS-03, extends existing feature); delivery note.
Expose wholesale transaction data in the Organizer panel for external invoicing; add absorbed-commission lines to the Fever→Organizer monthly invoice (reuses the manual flow).
Only timeless/standard/gift-card events appear (boxoffice excluded); default state on first publish; plan inherits marketplace price list at 0%.

rows.us: O-16 Create & manage distributor groups
rows.desc:
Create and manage distributor groups — exactly one group per partner per distributor. The group SELECTS WHICH PRICE LISTS APPLY to its distributors (the price lists on its channel) and drives exclusive-catalog visibility. Until a dedicated group exists, the public B2BM default group applies.

Group-creation wizard, event-first: create group → events → ticket types → decide what to publish where. The three price-list actions (keep the base list as-is, add the group's channel to a list, or create a new exclusive list) live in the per-event price manage view (multipricelist), NOT in the group wizard.

**A DISTRIBUTOR GROUP IS A SALES CHANNEL.** Settled 2026-07-08 ("a group IS a sales channel internally — new `b2b_marketplace` channel type, 1:1; 'group' is product copy only") and re-confirmed by Andrea on 2026-08-07: creating a group creates the Channel. That channel is the key the price list is scoped by.

**2026-08-07 — DISCOUNT VALUES ARE NOT SET HERE.** The B2B discount is edited from the price list (O-04 / B2BR-5154), not from the distributor group. This story owns WHICH lists a group's distributors resolve; it does not own what is on them.

**2026-08-07 — MOVING A DISTRIBUTOR BETWEEN GROUPS IS O-05 (B2BR-5155), NOT THIS STORY.** Both were claiming it, in the same milestone. This story creates and manages groups; O-05 moves a distributor from one to another.

**2026-08-07 — THIS WIZARD IS INDEPENDENT OF O-02 (B2BR-5152).** O-02 is the first-run modal shown when a new partner lands on B2B Publishing. Distributor groups work without it — the wizard there is preferable, not required. The dependency runs one way: O-02 needs groups, this story does not need O-02.

**2026-08-21 — RE-ESTIMATED 1 week -> "> 5 weeks" (5-6 dev-weeks), verified against fever2 and feverzoneclient.** What is already built: `b2b_marketplace` exists as a ChannelType (migration 2534, 2026-07-21) and price-list-to-channel scoping is complete (`PriceListChannel` + `PriceListsEvaluator`), so criteria 2, 3 and 4 are largely backend-done. What is NOT built, and is where the weeks are: (1) there is NO group construct to reuse anywhere — `Concession` is a pairwise grant, not a group, and `Channel` carries no partner/distributor reference, so criterion 1 is a new domain model plus a new uniqueness invariant; (6) rename and delete DO NOT EXIST — `ChannelAdmin.has_delete_permission()` returns False, there is no UpdateChannelCommand or DeleteChannelCommand, and `Cart.channel` / `Order.channel` are `on_delete=PROTECT`, so deleting a channel with history already raises ProtectedError; satisfying criterion 6 needs a new soft-delete / archive design with no pattern to copy. Frontend is net-new: the organizer-facing publishing UI lives in the ROOT Angular app, not in projects/b2b-marketplace, so the stepper engine must be reimplemented — 10-13 new components. Criterion 5 (default public group) has NO codebase evidence either way and is unscoped risk, not sized. Breakdown: backend model + uniqueness 1-1.5w · migration 0.25w · criterion-6 archive design 1-1.5w · criterion 5 ~0.5w discovery · frontend 2-2.5w.

⚑ 2026-08-21 — criterion 6 (rename/delete without orphaning bookings) is the candidate deferral: 1-1.5 dev-weeks, nothing to copy from, and nobody renames a distributor group in launch week. Deferring it takes O-16 to ~4 weeks, which is what returns milestone 3 to its target.

decisions.title: Visibility & access model (final)
decisions.note: Settled via the worked-example artifact. THREE plan access modes: OPEN (book immediately) · OPEN + REQUEST-ACCESS (visible to all, approval-required → request→approve→book) · EXCLUSIVE (offered to specific resellers; HIDDEN from everyone else — they never see it exists; NOT shown-but-locked, per Alejandro Herrero: see-but-can't-buy creates frustration). Per-reseller states: Bookable / Request access (🔒, only the open-to-all+approval case) / Hidden (🚫, an exclusive you're not on) / Removed (✕). Removal ops: BLOCK a distributor = cut them from ALL of one partner's events (unifies the former O-12 'revoke') + cancel pending reservations (confirmed kept, no new bookings); UNPUBLISH a plan for a reseller = pull one plan for one reseller (e.g. open→exclusive switch — confirmed kept, pending cancelled, open cart cleared); UNPUBLISH for everyone = pull from the marketplace (bookings stay payable). Card 'from' price = each group's lowest qualifying price, served either via a per-group materialized view OR a written 'from' field in FeverZone (materialization optional). Group = an exclusive offered to a SET of resellers — same hide mechanic, no separate model. Refines the 2026-06-23 pricing decision on the visibility dimension. — REFINED 2026-07-08: formalized as a relationship-state machine (Pending · Approved·Open-only · Approved·Full-catalog · Rejected); 'Hidden' is now expressed purely through group/channel publication, not a separate flag; per-distributor state is DERIVED from the relationship state + group publication. ⚠ UNDER REVISION 2026-07-09 — the catalog-request ↔ relationship governance is being reworked with design (mute/Ignored may be dropped for a terminal Rejected CTA).

decisions.title: Pricing structure: B2BM price-list inheritance + group model
decisions.note: ⚠️ REFINED 2026-06-26 by the 'Visibility & access model (final)' decision above — read together, not in isolation: point (2) 'catalog buyable by all distributors' holds only for OPEN events; EXCLUSIVE events are now HIDDEN from non-grantees (not shown-but-locked), and OPEN+REQUEST-ACCESS events are visible but approval-gated. So 'buyable by all' = the open catalog, not every event. — Original (validated 06-23): (1) A channel/group price list inherits from the B2B-marketplace price list, NEVER the generic base (retail-leak risk); the base is only the clone-source at creation. (2) The B2BM catalog is buyable by all distributors; group specificity = B2B discount per ticket + optional ticket-type-level visibility (aggregation, not inheritance). (3) MVP red-line: groups set only prices, no group-specific ticket types. Does NOT resolve the still-open 'auto-inherit global B2B discount?' or 'B2B discount min/max legal cap?' questions. — SUPERSEDED 2026-07-08 by the CLOSED price-list model: b2b-discount is a mandatory field on every price-list row (backfilled 0%); the winning list gives retail price + discount from the SAME row with NO fallback to a parent/base list (the earlier 'inherits from the B2B-marketplace list' mechanic is dropped); a group IS a sales channel. — CONFIRMED 2026-08-07 against fever2 `src/core/domain/price_list/`: PriceList.main_plan scopes a list to ONE event (never shared); applies_to_all_channels + the PriceListChannel join table do the channel restriction; PriceListItem.session_type makes the TICKET TYPE the pricing unit. Andrea re-confirmed a distributor group CREATES the Channel. ⚠ NOTE: PriceList.parent_price_list exists in the model, and a 2026-08-07 pass briefly wrote into SYS-01/O-04/O-16 that channel lists INHERIT through it — that was wrong and was corrected the same day. The 2026-07-08 closed model stands: single-row resolution, no parent fallback.

decisions.title: Does a new price list auto-inherit a configured global B2B discount?
decisions.owner: Answered by DEC-020 + DEC-036 + DEC-055 in model-documentation
decisions.note: Likely not — needs confirming. Also: how does the system resolve discounts when one price list spans multiple channels? — SHARPENED 2026-08-07: under the 2026-07-08 closed model the answer is NO by construction (no parent fallback). So the real question is the NO-ROW case: a distributor whose channel has no price-list row on an event has nothing to inherit. Do they resolve the default public B2BM group's row, resolve base retail at 0% discount, or see no price at all? O-04 is IN PROGRESS and will settle this by implementation unless it is decided first. Recorded on B2BR-5154 and B2BR-5282. — ANSWERED 2026-08-07, and it was already answered in model-documentation `resellers/b2bm/model/decisions.yaml`: DEC-036 adds a b2b-discount column to the BASE price list (backfilled); DEC-055 is most-specific-wins over the rows that exist, the winning row supplying retail + discount together with no parent fallback; DEC-020 makes 0% the catalogue's DAY-ZERO STATE (sells at retail, no B2B margin). Since the base list is always present and applies_to_all_channels defaults to true, there is no 'no row' state — a group without a dedicated row resolves the base at 0%. What remains open is DEC-020's second half: is a 0%/zero-commission sale legal with organizer consent, and is there a legal MAXIMUM discount — enforced in O-04's editor.

decisions.title: Wholesale reservation management at launch: customer info editable, cancel not available
decisions.owner: Andrea — with two open items below
decisions.note: Two decisions on the same evening that together reshape D-07. (1) CUSTOMER-INFO EDITING IS IN THE MVP FOR WHOLESALE, carved out of D-07b (post-MVP) into D-07a (B2BR-5160, Wholesales milestone). Customer is NOT the contact: per B2BR-5522 the contact is the booking distributor and the customer is the person attending, and the marketplace captures only one of them today. Wholesale needs it and commission does not, because on commission the Pay-by-Link captures the end customer at payment, whereas on wholesale the distributor buys inventory up front and resells afterwards, so the customer is often unknown at booking. (2) A DISTRIBUTOR CANNOT CANCEL — cancel was removed from D-07a, which is now view + edit customer info only. Together these make D-07a the ONLY way a wholesale booking reaches the right person: there is no cancel-and-rebook fallback. ⛔ AND IT IS BLOCKED: B2BR-5522 is a [Design]/b2bm-definitions ticket open since 2026-07-13, 'do not start until the customer/contact approach is closed', owner Spyros, approach reviewed but not closed. It owns WHERE customer information is captured, so there is nothing to edit until it lands, and it also gates D-08 (delivery note), likewise in the launch. Pulling this scope into the MVP converted a 28-day-stalled design ticket into a Wholesales-launch blocker. ⚠ THREE EARLIER RECORDS ARE NOW VOID: the D-07 split rationale (justified by cancel landing in the launch); D-14's deletion reason ('no change to be done', read as cancel reusing the existing refund path — there is no distributor cancel to reuse one); and DEC-025 (wholesale cancellation policy, open and unowned) which is either resolved by this or concerns a different actor. ⚠ STILL OPEN: can anyone cancel at all — the organizer path is described in no story and unsized as launch support load; and whether 're-share Pay-by-Link' survives on its own, having been bundled into the removed cancel criterion. ⚠ The substantive engineering work is TICKET RE-ISSUANCE, not the form: tickets are issued on payment (D-06/D-06b) and the resale happens after, so changing the customer must decide whether the issued ticket is reissued, its previous delivery invalidated, or both left live. Unspecified. ⚠ PERSONAL DATA: the customer is a third party with no Fever relationship whose details a distributor types in; lawful basis, retention and controller appear nowhere in the plan, nor in B2BR-5522's acceptance criteria. ⚠ EFFORT: D-07a's 1 week and D-07b's 2 weeks were an assistant division of D-07's original 3 weeks, never squad-sized. D-07a has since gained paid-order customer editing and ticket re-issuance and lost cancel. Deliberately NOT re-estimated — the Oct 12 / Oct 26 dates are unchanged on paper but now carry an un-priced change and a live blocker.

fzImpact.title: FeverZone impact
fzImpact.summary: Deposits lives inside FeverZone's reservation/cart engine end-to-end — creation, cart preview/modification, payment, cancellation and refund all gained deposit-awareness. The riskiest surface is the current “single main plan, two carts” approach: a deposit payment is a special order that must be excluded or special-cased in every order-based flow (partner order list, inventory, notifications, finance-billing, access-control, reporting). A “Payment/order decoupling” redesign (dedicated PaymentGroup/PaymentCharge entities, no Order created until settlement) is fully specced in the tracker as the long-term fix but is not yet an active build. Finance-billing gained a full deposit/settlement/credit-note domain (b2c + b2b) on the same PayableEntryRecordedEvent pipeline B2BM's commission work also uses.

refactors.change: Cart/Deposit entity split (source_cart → Deposit PENDING/PAID → remaining-amount recalculation); three settlement paths (Path A one-shot / Path B skip-to-full / Path C deposit-aware remainder) added to the existing reservation-payment endpoints so they stay deposit-aware without double-charging.

New pass-through item builders (DepositItemBuilder, RemainderItemBuilder) route by b2c_order.intent (DEPOSIT/SETTLEMENT/REFUND) through the existing reconciler→assigner→resolver pipeline; b2b_transaction rows + per-leg commission computation for reconciliation invoices.

Under the current approach, every order-based flow (partner order list, inventory session-type exclusion, notifications, access-control, reporting) must exclude or special-case “deposit orders” — flagged in the tracker as the main tech-debt/double-count risk driver.

~18 partner-export DAGs (SAP/CAPN, LivGolf, RAPI deliver exports, TBAI, United Parks, UNICEF, Rauda, Superfly, Bandsintown, etc.) individually assessed for deposit-line impact in the tracker; most affected only if/when a given partner needs a deposit line in their export (Data team owns; doesn't block rollout).

Eight known MVP limitations are explicitly documented (not blockers, but real gaps), and roughly 15 open finance/tax/legal questions remain unanswered in the tracker's own open-questions log.

deliveryPlan.title: Full Reservation Modification — shipped; legacy-flow cleanup + multi-slot FF retirement remaining
deliveryPlan.summary: Phases 0 (foundations/API contracts + concurrency guard) through 3 (increase/decrease, decrease-to-zero, adjustment editing, multi-timeslot/new sessions/packs, reschedule + performance) are all Done in Jira (B2BR-4555/4558/4767/4859/4807/4934) and live in production — 361 confirmed modifications in June. Progressive rollout (B2BR-5008): canary (fever4business, feveroriginals) → gradual expansion → opened to 100% of partners as of 2026-06-23, with Patrimonio Nacional explicitly excluded (its reservation-count rule breaks per-day limits with multi-slot bookings; the per-slot fix is deferred since the query must count paid + unpaid + cart slots). Remaining work: multi-time-slot feature-flag retirement (B2BR-5098 in progress, B2BR-5099 FE disclaimer in review, B2BR-4428 blocked) and the legacy-flow cleanup epic (B2BR-5182, to do — removes the enable_full_modification_flow flag and legacy modification code on BE/FE via child stories B2BR-5183/5184), which is explicitly gated on the rollout epic reaching 100% with no remaining fallback need.

rows.us: Full Reservation Modification — Foundations — Phase 0
rows.desc: Lay foundational data models and API contracts (POST /api/b2b/reservations/{id}/preview and /modify) to unblock parallel frontend work without altering existing backend logic or concurrency models. Sets up the FF_B2B_FULL_MODIFICATION feature flag.
rows.goal: OpenAPI/Swagger schemas + backend e2e behave files ready so Frontend can start integration immediately.

rows.us: Full Reservation Modification — Phase 1 — Increase/Decrease
rows.desc: Replace the legacy in-place-mutation pattern with the Immutable Cart Swap engine, secured by a new ReservationLockService (Postgres advisory locks) before any modification is allowed. Enables partners to increase/decrease existing ticket quantities, with implicit cancellation when a decrease reaches zero, and Pack (bundle) compatibility.
rows.goal: Modify a reservation without cancel-and-rebook, safely under concurrent booking/payment attempts.
acceptance: BDD tests pass: increase/decrease success, capacity exhaustion (409 + DB rollback), implicit cancellation (decrease to 0)
Concurrency test proves ReservationLockService queues concurrent Modify and Book requests without data corruption

rows.us: Full Reservation modification — Phase 1.1 — Decrease to Zero (Implicit Cancellation)
rows.desc: Reduce reservation item quantity, including the edge case where quantity reaches zero, which must trigger an implicit cancellation flow for that item/reservation (with a frontend warning/confirmation modal).
rows.goal: Quantity reductions never leave the reservation in an inconsistent state.
acceptance: Standard decrease (>0): total recalculated, availability updated, booking not cancelled
Decrease to 0: backend triggers cancellation flow, releases availability
Frontend shows a clear warning/confirmation modal before reducing to 0
All Behave scenarios for decrease + implicit cancellation pass

rows.us: Full reservation modification — Phase 1.2 — Adjustment Editing + Below 0 Scenarios
rows.desc: Preserve financial/commercial integrity during modifications involving manual price overrides (adjustments) and promo codes: adjustments recalculate/redistribute proportionally on modification; coupons are auto-removed (and the user notified) if a modification violates their eligibility rules; the final total is floored at 0 even though line-item balances may compute negative internally.
rows.goal: Discounts and adjustments stay correct and consistent through any modification.
acceptance: Existing CartAdjustment is cloned and redistributed via override_cart_prices() on the target cart
Coupon auto-removed + user notified if modification breaks its eligibility rules
Total is floored at 0; all calculations/validations run inside the same atomic transaction as the capacity check

rows.us: Full Reservation Modification — Phase 2 — Advanced Booking Modifications: Multi-timeslot, New Sessions & Packs
rows.desc: Consolidate three requirements into one unified modification flow: adding tickets for a different date/time (multi-timeslot), adding new ticket categories not in the original purchase, and full Pack (bundle) compatibility — built together since multi-timeslot and new-session-types share the same availability/selection flow, which gives Pack support “for free.”
rows.goal: One modification engine handles date changes, new ticket types, and packs — unlocks upsell without cancel-and-rebook.

rows.us: Full Reservation Modification — Reschedule & performance & monitoring
rows.desc: Move an existing booking from its original session (A) to a new one (B); alongside this, optimize the modification engine's performance and add observability metrics for system stability.
rows.goal: Reschedule works reliably at scale, with visibility into engine health.

rows.us: Rollout, Monitoring, and Documentation
rows.desc: Progressive Feature-Flag rollout of the unified flow (enable_full_modification_flow): Phase 1 canary on fever4business + feveroriginals to validate in-place reschedule and concurrency locks under real conditions, then Phase 2 gradual expansion to the rest of B2B partners. Backward compatibility + instant legacy fallback guaranteed throughout; standard observability (no bespoke MVP dashboards) plus basic operational documentation before Phase 2.
rows.goal: Ship the new flow to all partners without a big-bang cutover.

rows.us: Reservation Modifications opened to 100% of partners (Patrimonio Nacional excluded)
rows.desc: Opened to 100% of partners on a Monday 9am–12pm window. Patrimonio Nacional excluded: its max-reservations-per-day rule counts *reservations*, not *slots*, which breaks multi-slot bookings against a per-day limit. Per-slot fix deferred — the query must count paid + unpaid + cart slots, which is non-trivial.
rows.goal: Full-partner availability of the unified modify flow.

rows.us: Enable multi-time slot reservations for all partners
rows.desc: Unify the cart UI for increase/decrease on multi-time-slot reservations; fix the reschedule screen to pass all session_type_ids as an array (today only one is sent); display a clear “not supported” error on Modify for multi-slot (unsupported today); open the feature flag to all partners; delete FF-related code once stable.
rows.goal: Multi-time-slot reservations work end-to-end for every partner, not just flagged ones.

rows.us: Remove multi-slot feature flag: gate multi-time-slot support on the endpoint response + add a disclaimer in the rules view
rows.desc: Retire the standalone multi-slot feature flag by gating support on the endpoint's own response instead, and add a disclaimer to the reservation-rules view.
rows.goal: One less flag to maintain; clearer partner-facing messaging on multi-slot support.

rows.us: Full Reservation Modification — Remove legacy flow & retire the feature flag (cleanup)
rows.desc: Once enable_full_modification_flow is rolled out to all B2B partners and confirmed stable, remove the dead legacy modification code and retire the flag on both backend and frontend, so the new flow becomes the single, unconditional path. Precondition: do not start until the rollout epic (B2BR-5008) is complete with no remaining need for the legacy fallback.
rows.goal: Once `enable_full_modification_flow` has been rolled out to **all B2B partners** and the new flow is confirmed stable (rollout epic **B2BR-5008** complete), remove the now-dead **legacy modification code** and **retire the feature flag** so the new flow becomes the single, unconditional path — on both **backend** and **frontend**.

rows.us: [BE] Remove the legacy reservation-modification flow and retire the `enable_full_modification_flow` flag
rows.desc: Backend child story of the cleanup epic: delete the legacy modification code path and all enable_full_modification_flow branching.
acceptance: No reference to `enable_full_modification_flow` remains in the backend.
The legacy modification code paths are deleted; the new flow is the only backend path.
Test suite is green; legacy-only tests removed, new-flow coverage intact.
No dead imports / unreachable code left behind.
rows.story: As an engineer, I want to **remove the legacy reservation-modification backend flow and all** `enable_full_modification_flow` flag checks, so that the unified Full Modification flow is the single backend path and we stop maintaining dead code.

rows.us: [FE] Remove the legacy modification UI and the `enable_full_modification_flow` branching
rows.desc: Frontend child story of the cleanup epic: remove the legacy modification UI paths and flag-based branching.
acceptance: No reference to `enable_full_modification_flow` remains in the frontend.
The legacy modification UI is deleted; the new UI is the only path.
No dead components / unused assets / orphan translations left from the legacy UI.
Test suite is green; legacy-only tests removed, new-flow coverage intact.

decisions.title: Patrimonio Nacional excluded from the 100% rollout (per-day reservation-count rule)
decisions.note: Reservation Modifications opened to 100% of partners except Patrimonio Nacional — its max-reservations-per-day rule counts *reservations*, not *slots*, breaking multi-slot bookings against per-day limits. Per-slot fix deferred (the query must count paid + unpaid + cart slots, non-trivial). Proposed long-term fix: make the rule configurable (per-reservation vs per-slot, partner-level opt-out) — needs Alex Herrero to map which partners need which behavior, and a decision on whether to tackle this before or after the B2BM launch.

decisions.title: Seat modification × multi-time-slot / multi-plan: out of scope for now
decisions.note: Seat modification today overwrites the seat on a new slot; true multi-slot seat stacking is untested. Scope decision: the one-pager covers single-day/single-plan/single-slot only — multi-slot/multi-plan seat modification is future work (a full cart model is too large to take on now). Alejandro to ask Diego Carrasco (Games) about existing seating + multi-slot precedent.

decisions.title: Multiplan reservations: partner-escalated, proposed deferral to Q4
decisions.note: A partner escalated multiplan reservation modification as urgent (reached Frank and others). Proposal on the table: negotiate deferring multiplan + booking-questions modification to Q4 to protect the current release — multi-event reservations can't be modified today. Needs a review of all teams' deliverables before making the case.
